findings.severity: observation (medium for host and developer runs)
findings.title: A runner SIGKILL leaves its replay child and browser tree alive until the step ends
findings.evidence: runnerKill, 3 runs: the node child and the whole Chromium tree left 30.1 s after the kill with a 30 s step timeout, and 10.0 s and 10.0 s after it with a 10 s timeout (documents orphanWindowMs 90000; every process left together). Lifetime tracks the step timeout, not the kill. Code: studio-runner/src/run/child.ts, childRuntime.ts and launcher.ts hold no parent-death handling (no 'disconnect' listener; launcher.ts only listens for the child's 'exit').
findings.contrast: A guided browser dies with the runner: guidedWorkerKill, 3 runs, tree gone 0.31-0.33 s after the kill.
findings.ask: decide whether the replay child should exit when its IPC channel closes; until then the AC-11 k wording 'no orphaned browser tree' holds for the guided path and for cancel, not for a runner SIGKILL on a host. In a pod a killed container ends its processes [I; @devops to check].

findings.title: A duplicate POST /v2/runs is refused by capacity or by the backend admission, not by the runner
findings.evidence: duplicate leg: pool 1: the duplicate is answered 429 CAPACITY_SATURATED (the client classes it a retryable definite refusal); pool 2: the duplicate takes a slot, its admission is refused 409 by the backend CAS (observed-admission#1), the runner answers 503 and the client classes it AMBIGUOUS. Either way one replay child, one admission, one attempt. Code: runCoordinator.submitObserved has no execution-id duplicate check; the backend admission is the authority.

findings.title: What 'refused' means for a stale or late callback
findings.evidence: Replays after the run is over: observed-admission 409; earlier progress sequences 409; the last applied progress sequence 200 (idempotent echo); cross-run replays 400 or 403; guided: claim, outcomes and lifecycle 409, a repeated bootstrap-evidence 202 (idempotent echo). In every case the snapshot revision, ledger state, last_runner_sequence, attempt id, owner fence, action rows and (guided) the session document and progress are unchanged.

A real runner refuses the build and no browser reaches the origin. Lane F adapted publish()/learn() inside ObservedCoRunIT (about 230 lines, Publisher) instead of editing the fixture (outside its write set).

findings.title: A forced worker kill ends the in-flight guided action as UNKNOWN_OUTCOME at once
findings.evidence: guidedWorkerKill, 3 runs: sessionStateAfterKill UNKNOWN_OUTCOME 339, 359 and 343 ms after the kill; one action row; the killed runner got one dispatch and the new runner process none.
findings.owner: @qa (credits AC-11 'unknown actions stop as UNKNOWN_OUTCOME', live half)

findings.title: The guided session row keeps changing for a moment after a public cancel
findings.evidence: In 1 of 13 repetitions of the guided cancel case (corun07) a byte comparison of the session's document and progress, taken right after the browser tree left, differed from one taken after the replays. Waiting for three identical looks and teardownStatus CONFIRMED before the baseline made 13 of 13 repetitions pass (corun08 three, stress01 ten). I did not capture which field changed (the failing build had no field diff); the teardown confirmation writes progress.teardownStatus on its own thread after commit (GuidedSessionService.teardownAttempt) [I].
findings.owner: @qa (reading aid for any byte-for-byte comparison of a cancelled session)

findings.title: The public Run's principal is the Core user id, not the email
findings.evidence: Over the public routes the identity headers carry X-User-Id 'uid-<email>', so the secret-use entitlement for a public Run must be granted to that id. D3's IT grants the email because it calls the service directly. A harness that mixes the two gets 400 UNKNOWN_REFERENCE 'not a reference this CSI may use' (corun06).
